title: Intermediate microeconomics
audience: a college student in a finance, accounting or business degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Model consumer choice with utility and budget constraints, derive demand, model production and costs, analyze competitive markets, monopoly and oligopoly with game theory, and apply welfare analysis, uncertainty, information problems and externalities to real markets.

weeks.5: Costs in the short and long run
weeks.10: Choice under uncertainty and expected utility
weeks.11: Asymmetric information: adverse selection and moral hazard

blocks.deliverable: Decompose a price change into its two effects.
Derive a firm supply curve from a cost function.
Week 7 midterm; find the Nash equilibria of two games.
Explain a real market failure and one remedy.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Industry analysis: choose a real industry, describe its market structure, model one pricing decision with tools from the course, use game theory to explain competitive behavior, and write a three-page analysis of how the structure affects firms' profits.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
